request.spec:
Anyone using the app first signs in by typing a name; there is no password. The signed-in
name shows on the screen. A sheet is chosen by typing its id and loading it; the active sheet id
shows on the screen, and everything else in the app is kept per sheet. A sheet that has never been
loaded before starts empty. Everything happens on the one screen at /.

agent.result_text:
Sign-in and sheet loading now work, and `bin/e2e` passes (two users, uma and vic, each sign in and load the same sheet).

**How it works:**
- **Sign-in:** the start screen asks for a name. The name is trimmed and sent to `POST /api/signin`, which refuses a blank name with a 400. After sign-in the name shows in `current-user`, next to a Sign out button.
- **Sheets:** typing an id and pressing Load calls `PUT /api/sheets/{id}`. If the id has never been used, that creates an empty sheet; otherwise it leaves the sheet as it is. The id then shows in `sheet-current-id`. Loading a sheet also clears anything cached for it, so the screen re-reads it from the store, as the test's refresh helper expects.
- **Errors:** a refusal shows `signin-error` or `sheet-load-error` with the server's message, and the message goes away as soon as the field is edited. A blank sheet id now shows an error too; at first it silently did nothing. I checked the server refusals directly with curl, but no test covers these error paths.

**Design choices worth knowing:**
- The signed-in name and the active sheet are kept in the page URL as `?user=` and `?sheet=`, following the convention in `DESIGN.md`. So each browser tab is its own session, and a reloaded or shared link keeps both.
- I added a `sheet.body` slot (`src/main/frontend/slots/defs/sheetBody.ts`). It receives `{ sheetId, user }`, so later per-sheet features can be added without changing the screen itself.
- There's a shared way to refuse a request: throwing `BadRequestException` returns a 400 with an error message, which the front end displays.

**What I added:**
- A `sheet` table (Flyway `V1__sheet.sql`).
- The two endpoints, set up as YAML files under `officefloor/rest/api/`.
- Java classes in `net.officefloor.hq.app.session` and `.sheet`.
- On the front end, `features/session/` and `features/sheet/`, wired into `routes/index.tsx`, plus a `putJson` helper in `api/http.ts`.

Nothing writes to the audit file yet; this change doesn't call for any audit records.
